messages:
Maya Patel: quick sync 1 decomposition idea: split routing policy into match -> score -> enforce phases. safer rollouts, smaller hotpaths, but more RPCs. any red flags?
Ravi Singh: +1 on safety. need to define the minimal surface between match and score. if it's too chatty we'll tank p99.
Maya Patel: thinking match returns candidate route_ids + tiny attrs (region,tier,compat_flags). scorer pulls cost hints/telemetry to compute final score. route_ids must be stable across versions.
Liam O'Connor: stable ids are necessary. tenant overrides? can't query tenant DB synchronously per request.
Evelyn Park: cache overrides in a sidecar with TTL + invalidation on write. cheaper than per-request DB hits.
Andre Gomez: sidecar increases ops friction. alternative: edge includes a signed override vector per session (read once).
Maya Patel: signed overrides okay but adds crypto and trust boundaries. sounds feasible with short-lived signatures.
Ravi Singh: compress overrides into a versioned bitmask so validation is cheap in the scorer. keeps request size down.
Liam O'Connor: scoring should be functional (no side effects) so we can run it in-process for Dedicated flows. enforcement can be async and write audit events.
Evelyn Park: that separation makes testing easier; we can run a canary scorer in sim mode.
Andre Gomez: risk of divergence: in-process vs sidecar implementations must stay in sync; need integration tests.
Maya Patel: testing plan: property-based tests for scorer invariants + nightly trace replay against production traces. enforce scorer version pinning on rollouts.
Ravi Singh: policy authoring: current JSON blobs are messy. propose a compact DSL that compiles to stable opcodes; enables multiple runtimes (native / wasm).
Liam O'Connor: wasm for scoring is appealing (sandboxed, hot-reloadable). cold-start is a concern; cache compiled modules per host.
Evelyn Park: fallback to native scorer when wasm cold-start fails. explicit degrade path.
Maya Patel: wasm optional for tenant extensions/experiments. default native optimized path.
Andre Gomez: ops requirement: compatibility matrix mapping runtime versions to opcode sets. block or auto-translate old policies.
Ravi Singh: telemetry: scorer outputs structured enums (no free-form strings) for deterministic attribution.
Liam O'Connor: scorer should also emit cost_estimate and latency_hint fields so admission control can use them without recompute.
Evelyn Park: for preemption, expose a priority token from scorer. admission service consumes tokens to accept/reject under pressure.
Maya Patel: action items: (1) draft proto for match->score->enforce, (2) design stable route id scheme, (3) prototype DSL->wasm compiler, (4) build sim harness for nightly replays. i'll own API + IDs.
Ravi Singh: i'll own DSL + property tests.
Liam O'Connor: i'll prototype wasm bootstrap + module cache.
Evelyn Park: i'll mock sidecar override cache + invalidation semantics and run TTL experiments.
Andre Gomez: i'll draft ops playbook and compatibility matrix for rollbacks.
ops-bot: Deploybot: created epic "policy-decomposition-staging" (JIRA RD-7892) and assigned to Maya. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: can we aim for a first-pass proto by EOD Friday? want quick feedback loop.
Ravi Singh: i'll start a doc with concrete examples + contrived counterexamples to catch edge cases.
Liam O'Connor: ping infra when you have the wasm artifact, i'll add caching and warmup hooks.
Evelyn Park: note on metrics: avoid cardinality explosion if scorer emits tenant enums; default aggregation at route/region.
Maya Patel: include explicit fallback modes in proto: "exact" and "best_effort" so behavior is never implicit.
Andre Gomez: +1 for explicit.
Maya Patel: closing for now. will post proto link here when ready. :v:
